straits-settlements.t: British colony uniting Penang, Malacca and Singapore, the commercial hub of British Malaya for over a century.
straits-settlements.o: After the [[e:anglo-dutch-treaty-of-1824|Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1824]] secured [[s:dutch-malacca|Dutch Malacca]] for [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]], the [[e:east-india-company|East India Company]] in 1826 joined it with [[s:prince-of-wales-island|Prince of Wales Island]] ([[e:penang|Penang]]) and [[s:singapore|Singapore]] into a single presidency. The seat of government moved from Penang to [[e:singapore|Singapore]] in 1832.
straits-settlements.r: The settlements were ruled from [[s:british-raj|British India]] until 1867, when they became a crown colony under the Colonial Office, administered by a governor with executive and legislative councils. Free trade made [[s:singapore|Singapore]] a great [[e:entrepot|entrepot]] for [[e:tin|tin]], [[e:rubber|rubber]], opium and textiles. The governor also served as High Commissioner for the protected Malay states, and Chinese and Indian immigrants formed a majority.
straits-settlements.e: [[e:japan|Japan]] occupied the colony from 1942 to 1945. In 1946 [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] dissolved the Straits Settlements: [[s:singapore|Singapore]] became the separate [[s:colony-of-singapore|Colony of Singapore]], and [[s:prince-of-wales-island|Penang]] and [[e:malacca|Malacca]] joined the [[s:malayan-union|Malayan Union]], later becoming states of [[s:malaysia|Malaysia]].
straits-settlements.re: Sunni Islam, Chinese folk religion, Buddhism, Hinduism, Christianity

somali-republic.t: The first independent Somali state, formed by uniting the former British and Italian territories in 1960, and a parliamentary democracy until 1969.
somali-republic.o: On 1 July 1960 the [[s:state-of-somaliland|State of Somaliland]], independent for five days, united with the [[s:trust-territory-of-somaliland|Trust Territory of Somaliland]] to form the [[e:somalis|Somali]] Republic, with [[s:sultanate-of-mogadishu|Mogadishu]] as capital. Aden Abdullah Osman became provisional president and the constitution was approved by referendum in 1961, though many northerners voted against it.
somali-republic.r: The republic was a multi-party parliamentary democracy, among the more open in [[e:africa|Africa]], but politics was dominated by clan rivalries and patronage. It pursued the goal of uniting all [[e:somalis|Somalis]] in a Greater [[s:somalia|Somalia]], supporting insurgents in Kenya's Northern Frontier District, the Shifta War, and fighting a border war with [[s:federal-democratic-republic-of-ethiopia|Ethiopia]] in 1964. Abdirashid Ali Shermarke won the presidency in 1967.
somali-republic.e: On 15 October 1969 Shermarke was assassinated, and six days later the army under Mohamed Siad Barre seized power, dissolving parliament and creating the [[s:somali-democratic-republic|Somali Democratic Republic]].

samnite-league.t: Confederation of the Oscan-speaking peoples of the southern Apennines, Rome's toughest opponent in Italy during three Samnite Wars.
samnite-league.o: The Samnites lived in the mountains of modern Molise and inland Campania. They believed they descended from [[s:sabines|Sabines]] who had migrated south in a 'sacred spring'. By the 5th century BCE they had formed a confederation of four peoples, the Pentri, Caraceni, Caudini and [[s:hirpini|Hirpini]], with Bovianum as a main centre.
samnite-league.r: Each people (touto) was governed by an elected magistrate, the meddix tuticus, and the league acted together in war. Society was rural, living in villages and [[e:hill-fort|hill forts]]. The great sanctuary at Pietrabbondante, with its temple and [[e:theatre|theatre]], was a federal centre. Samnite warriors were famed for their armour, and their expansion carried Oscan speech into Campania, Lucania and Bruttium.
samnite-league.e: [[e:rome|Rome]] fought three Samnite Wars from 343 to 290 BCE. The Samnites trapped a Roman army at the Caudine Forks in 321 BCE but lost at Sentinum in 295 BCE and accepted Roman alliance in 290 BCE. They later backed Pyrrhus and [[e:hannibal|Hannibal]], and Sulla crushed them at the Colline Gate in 82 BCE.

shanghai-international-settlement.t: The self-governing foreign enclave at the heart of Shanghai, run by a council of foreign ratepayers, which made the city China's commercial capital.
shanghai-international-settlement.o: After Shanghai was opened to foreign trade by the Treaty of Nanking, a British settlement was laid out along the Bund in 1845 and an American one at Hongkou in 1848. In 1863 the two merged as the International Settlement, while the [[s:shanghai-french-concession|Shanghai French Concession]] stayed separate.
shanghai-international-settlement.r: The Settlement was governed by the Shanghai Municipal Council, elected by foreign property owners, with its own police and volunteer corps, while foreigners enjoyed extraterritoriality. Most residents were Chinese, but they had no seats on the council until 1928. Banks, trading houses and factories made it [[e:china|China's]] leading business centre, and the shooting of protesters by its police sparked the May Thirtieth Movement in 1925.
shanghai-international-settlement.e: [[e:japan|Japan]] occupied the Settlement in December 1941. In 1943 [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] and the [[s:united-states|United States]] renounced their rights to the [[s:nationalist-government|Nationalist government]], and Japan transferred control to the [[s:wang-jingwei-regime|Wang Jingwei regime]]; after 1945 it was fully Chinese.

sambians.t: Prussian people of the Sambian peninsula, the world's richest source of Baltic amber, whose conquest in 1255 led to the founding of Königsberg.
sambians.o: The Sambians lived on the Sambian peninsula between the Vistula and Curonian lagoons, in today's Kaliningrad region. Their amber had reached the Roman world, and in the [[e:vikings|Viking]] Age Scandinavian traders settled at Wiskiauten nearby. Adam of [[s:free-hanseatic-city-of-bremen|Bremen]] in the 11th century described the Sambians as humane people with much fur.
sambians.r: Sambia was the most populous and wealthy Prussian land, with nobles holding fortified seats and a strong warrior class. [[s:jaipur-state|Amber]], [[e:fur-trade|furs]] and slaves were traded across the Baltic. The Sambians kept the Prussian pagan religion and resisted Danish and Polish missions.
sambians.e: In 1255 a [[e:crusade|crusade]] led by King Ottokar II of [[s:kingdom-of-bohemia|Bohemia]] subdued Sambia, and the Teutonic Order founded Königsberg, named in his honour. The Sambians rose again from 1260 under Glande but were defeated. Many nobles joined the Order's service, and their land became Order territory and the [[s:bishopric-of-samland|Bishopric of Samland]].

state-of-eritrea.t: Africa's youngest state of the 20th century, won after a 30-year war with Ethiopia and ruled since independence by Isaias Afwerki.
state-of-eritrea.o: The Eritrean People's Liberation Front took Asmara in May 1991, ending the war that began in 1961 after the annexation of the [[e:eritrea|Eritrea]] federation. In a UN-monitored referendum in April 1993, 99.8 per cent voted for independence, which was declared on 24 May 1993, with EPLF leader Isaias Afwerki as president.
state-of-eritrea.r: The EPLF became the People's Front for Democracy and Justice, the only legal party. A constitution ratified in 1997 has never been implemented, and no national elections have been held. A border war with [[s:federal-democratic-republic-of-ethiopia|Ethiopia]] from 1998 to 2000 killed tens of thousands, and since then indefinite national service has driven many young Eritreans to emigrate. A 2001 crackdown silenced critics and the independent press.
state-of-eritrea.e: [[e:eritrea|Eritrea]] and [[s:federal-democratic-republic-of-ethiopia|Ethiopia]] signed a peace agreement in 2018, ending two decades of hostility, and Eritrean forces later fought in [[e:ethiopia|Ethiopia's]] [[s:tigray|Tigray]] war. The country remains a one-party state under Isaias, with Asmara as capital.

somalia.t: The Somali state since the collapse of 1991, rebuilt slowly through transitional governments into a federal republic still fighting al-Shabaab.
somalia.o: When Siad Barre fled in January 1991, the [[s:somali-democratic-republic|Somali Democratic Republic]] collapsed. Rival factions fought over [[s:sultanate-of-mogadishu|Mogadishu]], and famine in 1992 killed hundreds of thousands, prompting UN and US intervention, which ended after the Battle of Mogadishu in 1993. The north became the [[s:republic-of-somaliland|Republic of Somaliland]], and Puntland formed as an autonomous state in 1998.
somalia.r: A Transitional National Government formed in 2000 and a Transitional Federal Government in 2004. In 2006 the Islamic Courts Union took [[s:sultanate-of-mogadishu|Mogadishu]], provoking Ethiopian intervention, from which the militant al-Shabaab emerged. African Union troops of AMISOM, from 2007, helped push al-Shabaab out of Mogadishu in 2011. A provisional constitution in 2012 created the Federal [[s:somali-republic|Republic of Somalia]] with federal member states.
somalia.e: Somalia remains a federal republic with [[s:sultanate-of-mogadishu|Mogadishu]] as capital, governed by indirect elections among clan delegates, while al-Shabaab still controls parts of the countryside. Remittances, telecoms and livestock exports sustain the economy.

southern-xiongnu.t: The Xiongnu who submitted to the Han in 48 CE and settled inside China's northern frontier, where their descendants later founded the first of the Sixteen Kingdoms.
southern-xiongnu.o: In 48 CE Bi, a grandson of the shanyu [[e:huhanye|Huhanye]], led eight [[e:xiongnu-empire|Xiongnu]] tribes to submit to the [[s:han-dynasty|Han Dynasty]] and took the title of shanyu, splitting the [[s:xiongnu-empire|Xiongnu Empire]]. In 50 the Han settled his people in the frontier [[e:commandery|commanderies]] of the Ordos and northern [[e:shanxi|Shanxi]], with the shanyu's court at Meiji.
southern-xiongnu.r: The Southern Xiongnu kept their own shanyus and aristocratic lineages but were supervised by a Han official, the Protector of the [[e:xiongnu-empire|Xiongnu]], and received annual gifts of grain and [[e:silk|silk]]. Their cavalry fought for the Han against the [[s:northern-xiongnu|Northern Xiongnu]] and later in the Yellow Turban wars. Over time they took up farming and Chinese ways.
southern-xiongnu.e: In 216 [[e:cao-cao|Cao Cao]] detained the shanyu Huchuquan at Ye and divided the Southern Xiongnu into Five Divisions under Chinese supervision, ending the shanyu's independent authority. In 304 Liu Yuan, a descendant of the shanyus, founded [[s:han-zhao|Han Zhao]], the first of the [[e:sixteen-kingdoms|Sixteen Kingdoms]].

sendai-domain.t: The great northern domain founded by Date Masamune, third largest in Tokugawa Japan and leader of the northern alliance against the Meiji government.
sendai-domain.o: Date Masamune, who had sided with [[e:tokugawa-ieyasu|Tokugawa Ieyasu]] in 1600, began building Aoba castle at Sendai in 1601 and laid out the city around it. The domain was assessed at 620,000 koku, though its actual yield was much higher.
sendai-domain.r: Masamune developed [[e:rice|rice]] land on the Sendai plain and shipped surplus rice to Edo, and in 1613 he sent Hasekura Tsunenaga on an embassy to [[e:spain|Spain]] and [[e:rome|Rome]]. A long succession crisis, the Date disturbance of the 1660s, ended in a famous hearing before the [[e:shogun|shogunate]] in 1671. The domain had a large [[e:samurai|samurai]] class and maintained the Date family's cultural patronage.
sendai-domain.e: In 1868 Sendai led the [[s:ouetsu-reppan-domei|Ouetsu Reppan Domei]] in defence of Aizu but surrendered that autumn, and its lands were reduced. After abolition in 1871 it became part of Miyagi Prefecture.

serbian-hungarian-baranya-baja-republic.t: Leftist republic proclaimed in Pécs in 1921 as Yugoslav troops prepared to hand the region back to Horthy's Hungary.
serbian-hungarian-baranya-baja-republic.o: Yugoslav forces occupied Pécs and the [[e:coal|coal]]-mining region of Baranya in November 1918. The area became a refuge for Hungarian socialists, communists and liberals fleeing the White Terror. When the Treaty of Trianon returned the area to [[e:hungary|Hungary]], they proclaimed the Serbian-Hungarian Baranya-Baja Republic on 14 August 1921, with the painter Petar Dobrović as president.
serbian-hungarian-baranya-baja-republic.r: The republic was a last-minute attempt to stop the return of Horthy's regime, and hoped either for independence or union with [[e:yugoslavia|Yugoslavia]]. It had a provisional government and relied on miners' support, but had no means of defence once Yugoslav troops left.
serbian-hungarian-baranya-baja-republic.e: Hungarian troops entered Pécs on 21 and 22 August 1921, ending the republic after about a week. Thousands of its supporters fled to the [[s:kingdom-of-yugoslavia|Kingdom of Yugoslavia]], and the region returned to the [[s:kingdom-of-hungary-1920-1946|Kingdom of Hungary]] (1920-1946).

cr.a: National Assembly of the Republic of Serbia (Serbian Parliament)

sican.t: A theocratic culture of Peru's north coast, centred on the pyramids of Batán Grande, that dominated Andean goldworking and trade in arsenical bronze.
sican.o: The Sicán culture, also called Lambayeque, emerged around 750 in the La Leche and Lambayeque valleys, in the former territory of the [[s:moche|Moche]]. A legend recorded by the Spanish tells of Naymlap, who arrived by sea with a fleet of balsa rafts and founded a dynasty there.
sican.r: Middle Sicán, about 900 to 1100, was ruled from the Sicán Precinct at Batán Grande, with large adobe pyramids such as Huaca Loro. Elite tombs contained tonnes of grave goods, including gold masks and arsenical [[e:copper|copper]]. Sicán produced arsenical bronze on a large scale and used naipes, small copper axe-shaped objects, possibly as a form of currency. Trade reached [[s:republic-of-ecuador|Ecuador]] for spondylus shell. Its art centred on the Sicán Lord, a figure with winged eyes.
sican.e: Around 1100 a severe drought followed by El Niño floods led to the burning and abandonment of Batán Grande. Late Sicán continued at Túcume until the region was conquered by the [[s:kingdom-of-chimor|Kingdom of Chimor]] around 1375.

state-of-los-altos.t: Breakaway western highlands of Guatemala, recognised briefly as the sixth state of the Central American Federation before Rafael Carrera crushed it.
state-of-los-altos.o: Ladino and criollo elites of Quetzaltenango and the western highlands had long resented domination by [[s:republic-of-guatemala|Guatemala]] City. In February 1838, as Rafael Carrera's revolt shook [[e:guatemala|Guatemala]], they declared a separate state, and the federal congress recognised it in June 1838 as the sixth state of the [[s:federal-republic-of-central-america|Federal Republic of Central America]].
state-of-los-altos.r: Los Altos was a liberal government led by men such as Marcelo Molina, ruling a region with a large K'iche' and Mam Maya majority who had little say. It imposed taxes and levies that alienated indigenous communities, many of whom sided with Carrera. The state depended on the backing of Francisco Morazán and the federal army.
state-of-los-altos.e: After Morazán's defeat, Carrera invaded in January 1840, took Quetzaltenango and executed leading liberals, reincorporating the territory into the [[s:state-of-guatemala|State of Guatemala]]. A brief revival in 1848 also failed. The quetzal-bird emblem of Los Altos later appeared on [[e:guatemala|Guatemala's]] flag.

sulayhid-dynasty.t: An Isma'ili dynasty that united Yemen under the Fatimid banner and is remembered for Queen Arwa, one of the few women to rule in medieval Islam.
sulayhid-dynasty.o: Ali ibn Muhammad al-Sulayhi, a judge's son and Isma'ili missionary for the [[s:fatimid-caliphate|Fatimid Caliphate]], rose in revolt in the Haraz mountains in 1047. Within two decades he had taken Sanaa, Zabid and Aden and brought most of [[s:republic-of-yemen|Yemen]] under his rule, recognising the Fatimid [[e:caliphate|caliph]] in [[e:cairo|Cairo]].
sulayhid-dynasty.r: The Sulayhids spread the Fatimid mission to [[e:oman|Oman]] and western [[e:india|India]]. After Ali was killed by the [[s:najahid-dynasty|Najahid dynasty]], power passed to his son al-Mukarram Ahmad and then to Ahmad's wife, Arwa bint Ahmad, who governed from Dhu Jibla for some fifty years, built its great mosque and was given authority over the Fatimid mission in [[s:republic-of-yemen|Yemen]]. Governors such as the [[s:zurayid-dynasty|Zurayids]] ruled Aden for them.
sulayhid-dynasty.e: When the [[e:fatimid-caliphate|Fatimids]] split over succession in 1130, Arwa backed the infant al-Tayyib, founding the Tayyibi branch of [[e:ismailism|Isma'ilism]]. After her death in 1138 the state broke apart among the [[s:zurayid-dynasty|Zurayid dynasty]], the [[s:hamdanid-sultanate-of-yemen|Hamdanid sultanate of Yemen]] and others. Tayyibi leadership later moved to [[e:india|India]], where the Bohras continue it.

sambas-sultanate.t: Malay sultanate of north-western Borneo with Bruneian roots, whose lands drew Chinese gold miners and their self-governing kongsis.
sambas-sultanate.o: Sambas was founded in 1675 by Raden Sulaiman, a prince of Bruneian royal descent, who took the title [[e:sultan|Sultan]] Muhammad Shafiuddin I. He displaced an earlier Javanese-linked ruling house on the Sambas river, and the sultanate grew into the main Malay power of the north-western coast of [[e:borneo|Borneo]].
sambas-sultanate.r: The sultans ruled coastal Malay communities and drew tribute from Dayak villages inland. From the 18th century they invited Chinese miners to work the gold fields, but the miners formed powerful kongsis such as the [[s:heshun-confederation|Heshun Confederation]] that escaped the court. Sambas was attacked by the British in 1813 for harbouring [[e:piracy|pirates]].
sambas-sultanate.e: The [[e:dutch|Dutch]] made Sambas a protected state in 1818 and crushed the kongsis in the 1850s. [[e:sultan|Sultan]] Muhammad Ibrahim Shafiuddin was killed by the Japanese in 1944. The sultanate was absorbed into the [[s:indonesia|Republic of Indonesia]] in 1950; its palace survives in Sambas town.

senussi-order.t: A Sufi brotherhood that built a network of desert lodges across the eastern Sahara, led resistance to France and Italy and gave Libya its first king.
senussi-order.o: Muhammad ibn Ali al-Senussi, an Algerian-born scholar, founded his brotherhood in [[e:mecca|Mecca]] in 1837 and established its first lodge in [[e:cyrenaica|Cyrenaica]], at al-Bayda, in 1843. The order moved its headquarters to the remote oasis of Jaghbub in 1856 and later to Kufra, beyond the reach of the [[s:tripolitania-vilayet|Tripolitania Vilayet]].
senussi-order.r: The Senussi built zawiyas, lodges that served as schools, mosques, markets and courts, among the Bedouin of [[e:cyrenaica|Cyrenaica]] and along the [[e:caravan-trade|caravan routes]] to [[e:wadai-empire|Wadai]] and [[e:lake-chad|Lake Chad]]. Under Muhammad al-[[e:mahdi|Mahdi]] al-Senussi the order acted as a quasi-state, settling disputes, collecting religious dues and protecting trade, while preaching a reformed, austere [[e:islam|Islam]].
senussi-order.e: The Senussi fought [[e:france|France]] in [[e:chad|Chad]] from 1902 and [[s:italian-libya|Italian Libya]] from 1911; Omar al-Mukhtar led resistance until his execution in 1931. Allied with [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] in the [[e:second-world-war|Second World War]], Idris al-Senussi became ruler of the [[s:emirate-of-cyrenaica|Emirate of Cyrenaica]] in 1949 and king of the [[s:kingdom-of-libya|Kingdom of Libya]] in 1951.

second-empire-of-haiti.t: Haiti's second empire under Faustin I, a former soldier who crowned himself in imperial splendour and repeatedly failed to reconquer the Dominican Republic.
second-empire-of-haiti.o: In 1847 the Haitian senate chose Faustin Soulouque, an elderly and supposedly pliable general, as president. He soon turned on the mixed-race elite who had promoted him, killing opponents in Port-au-Prince in 1848. On 26 August 1849 he had himself proclaimed emperor as Faustin I, and he was crowned with great ceremony in 1852.
second-empire-of-haiti.r: Faustin created a court and nobility of princes, dukes and barons, ruled through the army and a feared militia, and tolerated [[e:haitian-vodou|Vodou]] more openly than his predecessors. The state monopolised [[e:coffee-economy|coffee]] purchases, and the economy suffered. He invaded the [[s:first-dominican-republic|First Dominican Republic]] in 1849 and again in 1855 to 1856, but was defeated at Las Carreras, Santomé and Sabana Larga, which cost him prestige.
second-empire-of-haiti.e: In December 1858 General Fabre Geffrard rose in revolt, and Faustin abdicated in January 1859 and went into exile. Geffrard restored the presidency, founding the modern [[s:republic-of-haiti-1806-1849|Republic of Haiti]].

state-of-aleppo.t: The French-created state of northern Syria around Aleppo, which existed for four years before being merged into the State of Syria.
state-of-aleppo.o: Following the defeat of the [[s:arab-kingdom-of-syria|Arab Kingdom of Syria]], the French high commissioner Henri Gouraud created the State of [[e:aleppo|Aleppo]] in September 1920. It covered northern [[s:syrian-arab-republic|Syria]] and the [[e:euphrates|Euphrates]] valley and included the [[s:sanjak-of-alexandretta|Sanjak of Alexandretta]], which had a special regime.
state-of-aleppo.r: The state was governed by local notables under French supervision; its first governor was Kamil Pasha al-Qudsi. [[e:aleppo|Aleppo's]] merchants suffered from the new borders, which cut the city off from its Anatolian hinterland after the 1921 Treaty of Ankara with [[e:turkey|Turkey]]. In 1922 the state joined the [[s:syrian-federation|Syrian Federation]].
state-of-aleppo.e: At the end of 1924 [[e:france|France]] merged the states of [[e:aleppo|Aleppo]] and [[e:damascus|Damascus]] into the [[s:state-of-syria|State of Syria]], effective January 1925, while Alexandretta kept its autonomy.

shilluk-kingdom.t: A kingdom of the Shilluk people on the White Nile, famous for its sacred kingship centred on the reth and the founder-hero Nyikang.
shilluk-kingdom.o: According to Shilluk tradition, the kingdom was founded by Nyikang, who led his people north along the White [[e:nile|Nile]] and settled them on its west bank. Historians date the establishment of the kingship to around the late 15th century, with Fashoda becoming the royal centre.
shilluk-kingdom.r: The reth was a sacred king, believed to embody the spirit of Nyikang; his health was linked to the wellbeing of the land, a case made famous by James Frazer and E. E. Evans-Pritchard. Settlements were dense along the river, living from [[e:sorghum|sorghum]], [[e:cattle|cattle]] and fishing. Shilluk canoe fleets raided as far north as the [[s:funj-sultanate|Funj Sultanate]].
shilluk-kingdom.e: In the 19th century slave traders and the [[s:turco-egyptian-sudan|Turco-Egyptian Sudan]] broke Shilluk power; Egyptian forces subdued the kingdom around 1861. Fashoda later gave its name to the Anglo-French crisis of 1898. The reth survives today as a traditional ruler in South [[e:sudan|Sudan]].

soppeng-kingdom.t: A Bugis kingdom in South Sulawesi, ally of Bone and Wajo in the Tellumpoccoe alliance against Gowa.
soppeng-kingdom.o: Soppeng was one of the Bugis kingdoms that formed in the fertile valleys of South [[e:sulawesi|Sulawesi]] from the 14th century, as [[e:rice|rice]] farming and trade grew. Its chronicles, written in the Bugis script, describe a founding in which a heavenly being, a tomanurung, was invited to rule by the leaders of the local communities.
soppeng-kingdom.r: Soppeng was governed by a datu advised by a council of local chiefs, and its wealth came from [[e:rice|rice]]. In 1582 it joined Bone and Wajo in the Tellumpoccoe, 'three powers', alliance against the expanding [[s:gowa-sultanate|Gowa Sultanate]]. Gowa forced it to accept [[e:islam|Islam]] in 1609.
soppeng-kingdom.e: Soppeng later sided with Arung Palakka of Bone and the [[s:dutch-east-india-company-territories|Dutch East India Company]] against Gowa in 1666 to 1669. It remained a [[e:dutch|Dutch]] ally under the Bone confederation until the Dutch conquered South [[e:sulawesi|Sulawesi]] in 1905 and brought its rulers under direct colonial control. It is now Soppeng Regency.
soppeng-kingdom.re: Sunni Islam, earlier Bugis indigenous religion

segusiavi.t: Gallic people of the Forez and Lyonnais on whose land Rome founded Lyon, the future capital of the Three Gauls.
segusiavi.o: The Segusiavi lived between the Loire and the Rhône, in the plains of the [[s:county-of-forez|Forez]] and the hills west of the Saône. Caesar describes them as the first people beyond the Rhône outside the Roman Province and as clients of the [[s:aedui|Aedui]].
segusiavi.r: Few details survive. Their territory commanded the crossing of the Saône and Rhône at the hill of Fourvière, a strategic point for trade between the [[e:mediterranean|Mediterranean]] and central Gaul.
segusiavi.e: They joined the revolt of 52 BCE with the [[s:aedui|Aedui]]. In 43 BCE the colony of Lugdunum (Lyon) was founded on their land, and their own chief town became Forum Segusiavorum (Feurs). Their name survives in the [[s:county-of-forez|Forez]] region.

smyrna-zone.t: The Greek-administered zone around Smyrna after the First World War, which ended in the destruction of the city in 1922.
smyrna-zone.o: With the approval of the [[e:allies|Allies]], Greek troops landed at [[s:smyrna|Smyrna]] on 15 May 1919, ostensibly to protect the large Greek [[e:eastern-orthodox-church|Orthodox]] population. The landing was marred by killings of Turks and helped ignite the Turkish national movement. The Treaty of Sevres of 1920 placed the zone under Greek administration, with a plebiscite on union with [[e:greece|Greece]] after five years.
smyrna-zone.r: The High Commissioner Aristeidis Stergiadis ran the zone and tried, with mixed success, to treat Muslims and Christians equally. A Greek university, the Ionian University, was planned under the mathematician Constantin Caratheodory. The zone served as the base for the Greek army's offensives deep into [[e:anatolia|Anatolia]] in 1920-1921.
smyrna-zone.e: After the Greek defeat at Dumlupinar in August 1922, Turkish forces entered [[s:smyrna|Smyrna]] on 9 September. A great fire destroyed the Greek and Armenian quarters, and the Christian population fled. The 1923 Treaty of Lausanne and population exchange confirmed the city's place in the [[s:republic-of-turkey|Republic of Turkey]].

state-of-grao-para-and-rio-negro.t: A short-lived Portuguese administrative state covering the Amazon basin, governed from Belém after the division of Grão-Pará and Maranhão.
state-of-grao-para-and-rio-negro.o: In 1772 the [[s:state-of-grao-para-and-maranhao|State of Grão-Pará and Maranhão]] was split in two. The western part, comprising the Captaincy of Grão-Pará and the Captaincy of São José do Rio Negro, created in 1755 with its seat at Barcelos, became the State of Grão-Pará and Rio Negro, governed from Belém.
state-of-grao-para-and-rio-negro.r: The state covered most of the Brazilian [[e:amazon|Amazon]]. Its economy relied on forest products such as [[e:cacao|cacao]], [[e:cloves|cloves]] and sarsaparilla gathered by indigenous workers under the Directorate system, and on trade through Belém with [[e:lisbon|Lisbon]]. Portuguese forts along the Rio Negro and Rio Branco guarded the frontier with Spanish territories.
state-of-grao-para-and-rio-negro.e: The separate state was short-lived; from the mid-1770s its captaincies were increasingly brought under the general government of [[s:new-republic-brazil|Brazil]]. Grão-Pará remained loyal to [[e:lisbon|Lisbon]] at independence and joined the [[e:brazilian-empire|Empire of Brazil]] only in 1823. The [[e:cabanagem|Cabanagem]] revolt shook the region from 1835 to 1840.

state-of-costa-rica.t: Southernmost member of the Central American Federation, a small, relatively stable state where coffee exports began to shape a distinctive society.
state-of-costa-rica.o: [[s:republic-of-costa-rica|Costa Rica]] joined the [[s:federal-republic-of-central-america|Federal Republic of Central America]] in 1824 after rivalry among its towns over joining [[s:mexico|Mexico]] had been settled by a brief civil war in 1823, after which the capital moved from Cartago to San José. Juan Mora Fernández became the first head of state.
state-of-costa-rica.r: Remote from the federal conflicts, [[s:republic-of-costa-rica|Costa Rica]] developed quietly under Mora Fernández, who ruled from 1824 to 1833. Small and medium farmers in the Central Valley took up [[e:coffee-economy|coffee]], which was exported to [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] from the 1830s, and the state encouraged planting with land grants. Braulio Carrillo, head of state from 1835, centralised power, defeated the rival towns in the War of the League and issued a decree of basic guarantees in 1841 that made him ruler for life.
state-of-costa-rica.e: [[s:republic-of-costa-rica|Costa Rica]] left the federation in November 1838 but kept the title of state. Carrillo was overthrown in 1842 by Francisco Morazán, who was himself executed months later. On 31 August 1848 José María [[s:duchy-of-castro|Castro]] Madriz proclaimed the Republic of Costa Rica.

sophene.t: Sophene, an Armenian kingdom in the upper Euphrates valley, ruled by a branch of the Orontid dynasty until Tigranes the Great absorbed it.
sophene.o: Sophene lay west of the [[e:tigris|Tigris]] sources around modern Elazığ, the old land of [[s:isuwa|Isuwa]]. In the 3rd century BCE an Orontid prince, Arsames, ruled it and founded Arsamosata. It was part of the wider Armenian world of the [[s:kingdom-of-armenia-orontid|Kingdom of Armenia (Orontid)]], though often under Seleucid overlordship.
sophene.r: Its kings controlled important crossings of the [[e:euphrates|Euphrates]] and [[e:tigris|Tigris]] and the routes between [[e:anatolia|Anatolia]] and [[e:mesopotamia|Mesopotamia]]. [[e:antiochus-iii-the-great|Antiochus III]] appointed Zariadres as governor; after [[e:rome|Rome]] defeated Antiochus in 189 BCE, Zariadres declared himself king. The court mixed Iranian and Greek traditions.
sophene.e: Around 95 BCE [[e:tigranes-the-great|Tigranes the Great]] of the [[s:kingdom-of-armenia-artaxiad|Kingdom of Armenia (Artaxiad)]] deposed its last king, Artanes, and annexed Sophene, uniting [[s:armenia|Armenia]].

saadi-sultanate.t: The sharifian dynasty that drove the Portuguese from much of Morocco, defeated them at the Battle of the Three Kings and conquered Songhai.
saadi-sultanate.o: The Saadis were a sharifian family from the Draa valley who rose in 1510 under Muhammad al-Qa'im as leaders of holy war against [[s:portuguese-morocco|Portuguese Morocco]]. They took [[e:marrakesh|Marrakesh]] from the [[s:hintata-emirate|Hintata emirate]] around 1525, captured Agadir in 1541 and [[e:fez|Fez]] from the [[s:wattasid-sultanate|Wattasid Sultanate]] in 1549, uniting [[s:kingdom-of-morocco|Morocco]] under Muhammad al-Shaykh.
saadi-sultanate.r: The Saadis kept [[s:kingdom-of-morocco|Morocco]] free of Ottoman control and built an army with firearms and renegades. In 1578 they crushed King [[e:sebastian-of-portugal|Sebastian of Portugal]] at Alcácer Quibir. [[e:ahmad-al-mansur|Ahmad al-Mansur]] grew rich from [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]] and Saharan gold, sent an army that destroyed the [[s:songhai-empire|Songhai Empire]] in 1591, and built the El Badi palace in [[e:marrakesh|Marrakesh]].
saadi-sultanate.e: After al-Mansur's death in 1603 his sons fought a long civil war, splitting the realm between [[e:fez|Fez]] and [[e:marrakesh|Marrakesh]]. Local powers such as the [[s:dilaiyya|Dila'iyya]] and the [[s:republic-of-sale|Republic of Salé]] rose, and the last Saadi was killed in 1659. The [[s:alaouite-sultanate|Alaouite Sultanate]] inherited [[s:kingdom-of-morocco|Morocco]].

state-of-grao-para-and-maranhao.t: Pombal's reorganised Amazon colony, ruled from Belém, where Jesuit control of indigenous peoples was ended and a monopoly company brought enslaved Africans.
state-of-grao-para-and-maranhao.o: In 1751 the Marquis of Pombal reorganised the [[s:state-of-maranhao|State of Maranhão]] as the State of Grão-Pará and Maranhão, moving its capital from São Luís to Belém. His brother Francisco Xavier de Mendonça Furtado became governor, charged with mapping the borders agreed with [[e:spain|Spain]] in the Treaty of [[e:madrid|Madrid]] and asserting royal power in the [[e:amazon|Amazon]].
state-of-grao-para-and-maranhao.r: Mendonça Furtado clashed with the [[e:jesuits|Jesuits]], who controlled indigenous villages and labour. In 1755 a law freed indigenous people from missionary rule, and from 1757 the Directorate placed their villages under lay directors and promoted Portuguese over the língua geral. The Jesuits were expelled in 1759. The General Company of Grão-Pará and Maranhão, founded in 1755, held a trade monopoly and imported enslaved Africans for [[e:cotton|cotton]] and [[e:rice|rice]] plantations.
state-of-grao-para-and-maranhao.e: In 1772 the state was divided into the [[s:state-of-grao-para-and-rio-negro|State of Grão-Pará and Rio Negro]] and the [[s:state-of-maranhao-and-piaui|State of Maranhão and Piauí]]. The trading company lost its monopoly in 1778. Its policies towards indigenous peoples shaped the [[e:amazon|Amazon]] for decades, and Belém remained the region's capital.

second-mexican-empire.t: The French-backed empire of the Habsburg archduke Maximilian, a monarchical experiment that ended with his execution at Querétaro in 1867.
second-mexican-empire.o: After French troops took [[e:mexico-city|Mexico City]] in 1863, [[e:napoleon-iii|Napoleon III]] arranged for an Assembly of Notables to offer the crown to Archduke Maximilian of [[e:austria|Austria]], brother of [[e:franz-joseph-i|Franz Joseph]]. Juan Nepomuceno Almonte headed a regency until Maximilian and his wife Carlota of [[s:kingdom-of-belgium|Belgium]] arrived in May 1864.
second-mexican-empire.r: Maximilian, a liberal, disappointed his conservative backers by upholding the Reform laws on church property and [[e:religious-tolerance|religious tolerance]], while seeking to protect indigenous communities. His power depended on French troops fighting Benito Juárez's republicans across the country. In 1865 his Black Decree ordered the execution of captured [[e:guerrilla-warfare|guerrillas]]. The empire was financed by heavy loans, and the court at Chapultepec Castle was lavish.
second-mexican-empire.e: After the American Civil War the [[s:united-states|United States]] pressed [[e:france|France]] to withdraw, and [[e:napoleon-iii|Napoleon III]] pulled out his army in 1866 to 1867. Maximilian stayed, was besieged at Querétaro and captured, and was shot with generals Miramón and Mejía on 19 June 1867. The republic was restored as [[s:mexico|Mexico]].

state-of-rui.t: A Ji-clan state on the Yellow River bend whose rich cemetery at Liangdai and outspoken minister Rui Liangfu make it one of the better-known minor Zhou states.
state-of-rui.o: Rui was a [[s:western-zhou|Western Zhou]] fief held by a branch of the royal Ji clan, its lords ranked as earls. It lay along the [[e:yellow-river|Yellow River]] where it divides Shaanxi from [[e:shanxi|Shanxi]], near modern Ruicheng and later at Liangdai village by Hancheng.
state-of-rui.r: Earl Rui Liangfu served at the royal court and is remembered for warning King Li of Zhou against monopolising the kingdom's resources. In 709 BCE Earl Wan of Rui was driven out by his mother, Rui Jiang, and the states of [[e:qin-dynasty|Qin]] and Jin intervened. The Liangdai cemetery, excavated from 2005, yielded fine jades and gold ornaments.
state-of-rui.e: Wedged between rising [[e:qin-dynasty|Qin]] and Jin, Rui was annexed by the [[s:state-of-qin|State of Qin]] in 640 BCE as Qin pushed east towards the [[e:yellow-river|Yellow River]].

sharkha-sultanate.t: A small Muslim principality of the south-eastern Ethiopian highlands, listed among the seven Muslim states of medieval Abyssinia.
sharkha-sultanate.o: Sharkha is known almost only from the 14th-century Arab geographer [[e:al-umari|al-Umari]], who named it among the seven Muslim kingdoms of Abyssinia. It probably lay in the Arsi highlands, between [[s:hadiya-sultanate|Hadiya]] and [[e:bale|Bale]], in a region of farming and [[e:cattle|cattle]] herding settled by Muslim communities along the trade routes.
sharkha-sultanate.r: [[e:al-umari|Al-Umari]] describes it as a modest state with a small army, whose people grew crops and kept livestock. After the campaigns of [[e:amda-seyon-i|Amda Seyon]] in the 1330s it paid tribute to the [[s:ethiopian-empire|Ethiopian Empire]], though its local Muslim rulers kept their positions.
sharkha-sultanate.e: Sharkha fades from the record in the 15th century. Its lands were later caught up in the wars of the [[s:adal-sultanate|Adal Sultanate]] and then settled by [[e:oromo|Oromo]] groups during the migrations of the 16th century.

sohawal-state.t: A Baghel Rajput state of Baghelkhand, founded by a younger son of the Rewa ruling house and later itself split into smaller holdings.
sohawal-state.o: Sohawal was founded around 1550 by Fateh Singh, a younger son of the Baghel ruler of Rewa, who received lands near the Satna river as his share. Like many cadet branches in [[s:rewa-state|Baghelkhand]], it became a separate principality while acknowledging kinship with Rewa State.
sohawal-state.r: The Raja ruled a small agrarian territory of villages and jungle. Over time the state lost land to relatives, and [[s:kothi-state|Kothi State]] emerged as a separate holding from the same family. In the British period Sohawal was a non-salute state under the [[s:rewa-state|Baghelkhand]] Agency.
sohawal-state.e: Its last ruler acceded to [[e:india|India]] in 1947, and in 1948 Sohawal was merged into [[s:vindhya-pradesh|Vindhya Pradesh]], which itself became part of Madhya Pradesh in 1956. Its lands lie in today's Satna district.

sidon.t: Sidon, one of the oldest Phoenician cities, whose kings led the Persian navy and whose name long stood for all Phoenicians.
sidon.o: Sidon stood on a promontory with offshore islets forming a harbour on the southern Lebanese coast. Inhabited since prehistory, it was a Canaanite port in the [[e:akhetaten|Amarna]] age, and in Homer and the Bible Sidonians means [[e:phoenicians|Phoenicians]] in general, a sign of its early prestige.
sidon.r: Its kings ruled a merchant city famous for glass and purple cloth, and honoured the healing god Eshmun at a great sanctuary outside the city. Under the [[s:achaemenid-empire|Achaemenid Empire]] Sidon was the leading Phoenician city and supplied the core of the Persian fleet; the inscribed sarcophagus of Eshmunazar II survives.
sidon.e: [[e:esarhaddon|Esarhaddon]] of the [[s:assyrian-empire|Assyrian Empire]] razed the city in 677 BCE, and [[e:artaxerxes-iii|Artaxerxes III]] burned it again after King Tennes rebelled. In 332 BCE Sidon opened its gates to Alexander of the [[s:macedonian-empire|Macedonian Empire]], who installed Abdalonymus as king, ending its independent history.

syrian-federation.t: A short-lived federation of the French-created Syrian states, a step towards reuniting Syria under the mandate.
syrian-federation.o: In June 1922 the French high commissioner Henri Gouraud united the [[s:state-of-damascus|State of Damascus]], the [[s:state-of-aleppo|State of Aleppo]] and the [[s:alawite-state|Alawite State]] in a federation, a partial response to nationalist demands for unity.
syrian-federation.r: A federal council of delegates from the three states, under the presidency of Subhi Barakat, handled common affairs, while each state kept its own government and French officials held real power. The capital alternated between [[e:aleppo|Aleppo]] and [[e:damascus|Damascus]]. The federation had a single budget, customs and currency, but nationalists criticised it as a French device that kept [[s:lebanese-republic|Lebanon]], the Jabal Druze and Alexandretta apart from [[s:syrian-arab-republic|Syria]]. The [[s:alawite-state|Alawite State]] withdrew at the start of 1925.
syrian-federation.e: At the end of 1924 [[e:france|France]] dissolved the federation, merging [[e:damascus|Damascus]] and [[e:aleppo|Aleppo]] into the [[s:state-of-syria|State of Syria]] from January 1925.

sultanate-of-lahej.t: The Abdali sultanate north of Aden, which lost Aden to Britain in 1839 but remained the leading state of the Aden hinterland.
sultanate-of-lahej.o: The Abdali tribe held the fertile Lahej oasis north of Aden. Around 1728, under [[e:sultan|Sultan]] Fadl ibn Ali, they rejected the authority of the [[s:qasimid-state|Qasimid State]] and founded an independent sultanate, which also took control of the port of Aden.
sultanate-of-lahej.r: Lahej lived on irrigated agriculture and the trade passing between Aden and the interior. In 1839 the British [[e:east-india-company|East India Company]] seized Aden from [[e:sultan|Sultan]] Muhsin ibn Fadl, creating the [[s:aden-settlement|Aden Settlement]], and Lahej became the most important of the protected states around it. Ottoman forces occupied Lahej in 1915-1918. The sultanate's court was a centre of poetry and song, notably under Ahmad Fadl al-Qumandan.
sultanate-of-lahej.e: [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] deposed [[e:sultan|Sultan]] Ali ibn Abd al-Karim in 1958 for his nationalist contacts. Lahej joined the [[s:federation-of-south-arabia|Federation of South Arabia]], and in 1967 the National Liberation Front took over, abolishing the sultanate within [[s:south-yemen|South Yemen]].

sultanate-of-zanzibar.t: An Omani Arab sultanate on the islands of Zanzibar and Pemba, once the commercial capital of East Africa and its greatest slave and clove market.
sultanate-of-zanzibar.o: Sayyid Said of [[e:oman|Oman]] moved his court to Zanzibar in the 1830s and 1840s, building an empire of clove plantations and coastal trading posts. When he died in 1856 his sons divided his realm, and Majid became sultan of Zanzibar. The Canning Award of 1861, arranged by [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]], confirmed its separation from Oman.
sultanate-of-zanzibar.r: The sultans ruled the islands and claimed the coast from [[s:somalia|Somalia]] to [[s:portuguese-mozambique|Mozambique]]. The economy rested on clove plantations worked by enslaved Africans and on caravans bringing [[e:ivory-trade|ivory]] and slaves from the interior. Under British pressure [[e:sultan|Sultan]] Barghash closed the slave market in 1873. Arab, [[e:swahili|Swahili]], Indian and African communities created a cosmopolitan town, now Stone Town.
sultanate-of-zanzibar.e: European partition stripped away the mainland, and in 1890 Zanzibar became a British [[e:protectorate|protectorate]]. The Anglo-Zanzibar War of 1896 lasted under an hour. It became independent in December 1963 under [[e:sultan|Sultan]] Jamshid bin Abdullah, but the revolution of January 1964 created the [[s:peoples-republic-of-zanzibar|People's Republic of Zanzibar]].

siphnos.t: Cycladic island that grew briefly rich on gold and silver mines and built a celebrated treasury at Delphi.
siphnos.o: Siphnos, in the western Cyclades, was settled by [[e:ionia|Ionian Greeks]] from [[s:athens|Athens]] in the early Iron Age. Its [[e:silver|silver]] and gold deposits, worked since the [[e:bronze-age|Bronze Age]], made it in the 6th century BCE the richest island of the [[e:aegean|Aegean]], according to [[e:herodotus|Herodotus]].
siphnos.r: Siphnians shared their mining income as citizens and gave a tithe to [[s:delphi|Delphi]], where they built the Siphnian Treasury c. 525 BCE, with its famous sculpted frieze. Exiles from [[s:samos|Samos]] extorted a hundred [[e:talent|talents]] from the island c. 524 BCE. Siphnos later sent a ship to Salamis and paid tribute in the [[s:delian-league|Delian League]].
siphnos.e: The mines failed, flooded by the sea, which legend blamed on the Siphnians cheating Apollo of his tithe. The island remained a modest community known for its pottery under Hellenistic powers and [[e:rome|Rome]], losing independence by 146 BCE.

silvanectes.t: Small Gallic people of the forests north of Paris whose town Augustomagus became Senlis.
silvanectes.o: The Silvanectes are not named by Caesar and were probably part of the [[s:suessiones|Suessiones]] during the conquest. Pliny and Ptolemy record them as a separate people between the [[s:parisii|Parisii]], [[s:bellovaci|Bellovaci]] and Suessiones.
silvanectes.r: Their name has been linked to the forests of the Oise, but nothing is recorded of their society.
silvanectes.e: Under [[e:rome|Rome]] they formed a civitas with Augustomagus (Senlis) as its chief town. It became a bishopric and in 987 the assembly at Senlis elected Hugh Capet king, founding the [[s:kingdom-of-france|Kingdom of France]].

sultanate-of-ouargla.t: An oasis sultanate in the Algerian Sahara, ruling Ouargla's palm groves at a crossroads of caravan routes between the Maghreb and the Sahel.
sultanate-of-ouargla.o: Ouargla had been an Ibadi and trading centre since the early Middle Ages, near the ruined city of Sedrata. A local sultanate is attested from around 1500, when chroniclers such as [[e:leo-africanus|Leo Africanus]] describe the town as a wealthy caravan stop with its own ruler.
sultanate-of-ouargla.r: The sultans had limited power, mediating between the town's factions, the surrounding nomadic tribes such as the Chaamba, and Berber-speaking oasis farmers. The economy rested on date palms, irrigation and trade in slaves, gold and goods between the [[e:mediterranean|Mediterranean]] and the [[e:sahel|Sahel]]. Ouargla paid tribute at times to the [[s:regency-of-algiers|Regency of Algiers]] and competed with the [[s:sultanate-of-touggourt|Sultanate of Touggourt]].
sultanate-of-ouargla.e: The French extended their influence in the 1850s, and [[s:french-algeria|French Algeria]] occupied Ouargla in 1872, ending the sultanate. The town later became the centre of the Algerian oil industry.

sachin-state.t: A small Siddi Nawabi state near Surat, created when a claimant to Janjira gave up his rights in exchange for land.
sachin-state.o: The [[e:siddis|Siddis]], of East African descent, ruled the island fortress of Janjira on the [[e:konkan-coast|Konkan coast]]. In 1791, after a succession dispute, the [[e:peshwa|Peshwa's]] government arranged for the claimant Abdul Karim Yakut Khan to renounce Janjira in return for the lands of Sachin near [[e:surat|Surat]].
sachin-state.r: Sachin was a 9-gun salute state ruled by a Nawab under the [[e:surat|Surat]] Agency, later the [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]] States Agency, with a mostly [[e:hinduism|Hindu]] farming population.
sachin-state.e: After accession to [[e:india|India]] Sachin was merged into Bombay State in 1948 and has been part of [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]] since 1960; the area is now a suburb of [[e:surat|Surat]].

sakai.t: A self-governing merchant port near Osaka that Jesuit visitors compared to Venice, a centre of overseas trade, gunmaking and the tea ceremony.
sakai.o: Sakai grew as a port on Osaka Bay and became a terminus of the official trade with Ming [[e:china|China]] after the Onin War made the routes through Hyogo unsafe from about 1469. Wealthy merchant houses took over the town's administration as central authority collapsed.
sakai.r: A council of leading merchants, the egoshu, governed the town, which was protected by moats and hired its own guards. Sakai traded with [[e:china|China]], the [[s:ryukyu-kingdom|Ryukyu Kingdom]] and later the Portuguese, and became one of [[e:japan|Japan's]] main producers of firearms. The [[e:tea|tea]] masters Takeno Joo and Sen no Rikyu came from its merchant class, and the [[e:jesuits|Jesuit]] Gaspar Vilela described it as a republic like [[e:venice|Venice]].
sakai.e: In 1568 [[e:oda-nobunaga|Oda Nobunaga]] demanded a huge war levy; Sakai at first resisted but submitted in 1569 and came under his direct control. [[e:toyotomi-hideyoshi|Toyotomi Hideyoshi]] later filled in its moats and moved many merchants to Osaka.

serbia-and-montenegro.t: Loose union of Serbia and Montenegro that replaced the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and ended when Montenegro voted for independence.
serbia-and-montenegro.o: By 2001 Montenegro's government sought independence from the [[s:federal-republic-of-yugoslavia|Federal Republic of Yugoslavia]]. To avoid a sudden break, the [[e:european-union|European Union]], through Javier Solana, brokered the [[e:belgrade|Belgrade]] Agreement of 2002. A Constitutional Charter adopted on 4 February 2003 turned the federation into the State Union of [[e:serbia|Serbia]] and [[s:montenegro|Montenegro]], with Belgrade as its seat.
serbia-and-montenegro.r: The union had a single-chamber parliament, a president, Svetozar Marović, and a small council of ministers handling foreign affairs, defence and human rights. Otherwise the two republics ran their own affairs: [[s:montenegro|Montenegro]] used the euro and [[s:serbia|Serbia]] the dinar, with separate customs systems. The charter allowed either member to hold an independence referendum after three years.
serbia-and-montenegro.e: In a referendum on 21 May 2006, 55.5 percent of Montenegrin voters chose independence, just above the 55 percent threshold set by the EU. [[s:montenegro|Montenegro]] declared independence on 3 June 2006, and [[s:serbia|Serbia]] became the union's legal successor.

sogn.t: Petty kingdom around the Sognefjord, Norway's longest fjord, absorbed into Harald Fairhair's realm in the late 9th century.
sogn.o: Sogn, the land around the great Sognefjord in western [[e:norway|Norway]], appears in the sagas as one of the small kingdoms of the [[e:vikings|Viking]] Age. Rich graves along the fjord show a prosperous elite in the Iron Age, but its rulers are known only from late Icelandic tradition.
sogn.r: Its people farmed the fjord slopes, raised livestock in mountain pastures and traded along the coast and over the mountains to eastern [[e:norway|Norway]]. The site of the Gulating, the great law assembly of western Norway, lay at Gulen near the mouth of the fjord, and the district later belonged to its law province.
sogn.e: The sagas say Harald Fairhair took Sogn during his conquest of the west coast and placed it under one of his earls. It became part of the [[s:kingdom-of-norway|Kingdom of Norway]]; in the Middle Ages Sogn was known for its stave churches, including Urnes, now a World Heritage Site.

state-of-maranhao-and-piaui.t: A short-lived Portuguese administrative state on Brazil's northern coast, governed from São Luís after the division of Grão-Pará and Maranhão in 1772.
state-of-maranhao-and-piaui.o: When the [[s:state-of-grao-para-and-maranhao|State of Grão-Pará and Maranhão]] was divided in 1772, the eastern part, made up of the captaincies of Maranhão and Piauí, became the State of Maranhão and Piauí, with its capital at São Luís.
state-of-maranhao-and-piaui.r: Maranhão grew [[e:cotton|cotton]] and [[e:rice|rice]] for export on plantations worked by enslaved Africans, many imported by the General Company of Grão-Pará and Maranhão, and São Luís prospered as a port. Piauí, with its capital at Oeiras, was a land of [[e:cattle|cattle]] ranches supplying meat to the northeast. Little is known of the state's separate administration.
state-of-maranhao-and-piaui.e: The separate state was soon merged back into the general administration of [[s:new-republic-brazil|Brazil]], and its captaincies became provinces after 1821. Maranhão stayed loyal to Portugal at independence and joined the [[e:brazilian-empire|Empire of Brazil]] only in 1823. Piauí and Maranhão are today states of [[e:brazil|Brazil]].

sama-kaabu.t: One of the three royal provinces of the Kaabu Empire, whose Nyancho nobles took turns supplying the empire's ruler.
sama-kaabu.o: Sama was a province of the [[e:mandinka|Mandinka]] [[s:kaabu-empire|Kaabu Empire]] in present-day [[e:guinea-bissau|Guinea-Bissau]], which grew out of the westward expansion of the [[s:mali-empire|Mali Empire]] and became independent in the 16th century. [[e:kaabu-empire|Kaabu's]] history is known mainly from oral tradition and a few Portuguese accounts.
sama-kaabu.r: Sama, [[s:pachana-kaabu|Pachana]] and [[s:jimara-kaabu|Jimara]] were the three royal provinces whose Nyancho warrior aristocracy, traced through the female line, provided the Mansaba, the supreme king of [[e:kaabu-empire|Kaabu]], in rotation. Each was ruled by its own [[e:mansa|mansa]]. The Nyancho lived largely from [[e:slave-raiding|slave raiding]] and trade with Portuguese ports.
sama-kaabu.e: Sama declined with [[e:kaabu-empire|Kaabu]] in the 19th century under [[e:fula|Fulani]] attacks from the [[s:imamate-of-futa-jallon|Imamate of Futa Jallon]]. After the fall of [[e:kansala|Kansala]] in 1867 the province was absorbed into Fula-ruled states and later [[s:portuguese-guinea|Portuguese Guinea]].

samos-empire.t: The first known Slavic political union, led by the Frankish merchant Samo, which threw off Avar rule and defeated a Frankish king.
samos-empire.o: Around 623 the [[e:slavs|Slavs]] of central [[e:europe|Europe]], called Wends in the Chronicle of Fredegar, rebelled against their [[e:avars|Avar]] overlords. Samo, a Frankish merchant trading with them, fought so well that they chose him as king. The location of his realm is debated, but it probably covered [[s:kingdom-of-bohemia|Bohemia]], [[s:great-moravia|Moravia]], parts of Slovakia and Lower [[e:austria|Austria]].
samos-empire.r: Fredegar, the only substantial source, reports that Samo ruled for 35 years, had twelve Slavic wives and won every battle against the [[e:avars|Avars]]. In 631 a dispute over murdered Frankish merchants led King Dagobert I to invade; Samo defeated the [[s:franks|Franks]] at Wogastisburg, and the Sorb prince Dervan then joined him.
samos-empire.e: After Samo's death around 658 his union seems to have dissolved, and nothing more is heard of it; the [[e:avars|Avars]] regained influence in the region. It is remembered as a forerunner of later Slavic states such as [[s:great-moravia|Great Moravia]] and [[s:carantania|Carantania]], though no direct continuity is known.

state-of-nicaragua.t: Member state of the Central American Federation, crippled by the feud between liberal León and conservative Granada.
state-of-nicaragua.o: [[s:republic-of-nicaragua|Nicaragua]] became a state of the [[s:federal-republic-of-central-america|Federal Republic of Central America]] after the fall of the [[s:first-mexican-empire|First Mexican Empire]]. It adopted its constitution in 1826, with León as capital, but its towns had already fought each other in 1824 over who should hold power.
state-of-nicaragua.r: The rivalry between León, seat of liberal lawyers and officials, and [[e:granada|Granada]], home of conservative merchants trading through Lake [[s:republic-of-nicaragua|Nicaragua]] and the San Juan River, produced repeated civil wars. Heads of state rarely lasted: Manuel Antonio de la Cerda was executed in 1828, and José Zepeda was murdered in 1837. [[e:cattle|Cattle]] ranching and [[e:cacao|cacao]] sustained a small economy, while the British-allied Miskito controlled the [[e:caribbean|Caribbean]] coast.
state-of-nicaragua.e: A constituent assembly declared [[s:republic-of-nicaragua|Nicaragua]] independent of the federation on 30 April 1838, the first state to leave, creating the Republic of Nicaragua. León and [[e:granada|Granada]] carried their feud into the new republic, and the coastal Miskito remained outside its control.

sestos.t: Greek city on the European shore of the Hellespont, key to the grain route, whose capture by Athens in 478 BCE closes Herodotus's Histories.
sestos.o: Sestos was founded by Aeolian settlers from Lesbos on the Thracian Chersonese, at the narrows of the [[e:hellespont|Hellespont]] opposite [[s:abydos|Abydos]]. Its harbour and position made it the main crossing point from [[e:asia|Asia]] into [[e:europe|Europe]].
sestos.r: Sestos lay near the site of [[e:xerxes-i|Xerxes's]] bridges in 480 BCE. In 479 to 478 BCE the Athenians under Xanthippus besieged and took it, the episode that ends [[e:herodotus|Herodotus's]] Histories. It became a key Athenian base for protecting the [[e:black-sea|Black Sea]] grain route and paid tribute in the [[s:delian-league|Delian League]]. Greek legend made it the home of Hero, beloved of Leander.
sestos.e: After the Athenian defeat at nearby Aegospotami in 405 BCE, Sestos passed to [[s:sparta|Sparta]], then back to [[s:athens|Athens]] and later to Macedonian and Hellenistic rulers. It came under Roman control by 146 BCE.

scordisci.t: Celtic people at the meeting of the Sava and Danube who founded Singidunum, modern Belgrade, and harried Roman Macedonia for two centuries.
scordisci.o: After the Celtic [[e:second-persian-invasion-of-greece|invasion of Greece]] under Brennus failed in 279 BCE, survivors settled at the confluence of the Sava and [[e:danube|Danube]]. There they merged with local Illyrian and Thracian peoples and formed the Scordisci, with strongholds at Singidunum ([[e:belgrade|Belgrade]]) and Taurunum (Zemun).
scordisci.r: A warrior aristocracy ruled over a mixed population, dominating the middle [[e:danube|Danube]] from fortified oppida. They minted coins, traded along the river and raided south. In 114 BCE they destroyed a Roman army under Gaius Porcius Cato in Macedonia, and wars with [[e:rome|Rome]] followed for decades. The Dacian king Burebista defeated them in the mid-1st century BCE.
scordisci.e: Tiberius subdued the Scordisci during his Pannonian campaigns of 12–9 BCE, and they became allies of [[e:rome|Rome]]. By the early 1st century CE they were absorbed into the provinces of [[e:pannonia|Pannonia]] and Moesia, and the name Singidunum survived as a Roman [[e:legion|legionary]] base.

state-of-xing.t: A Zhou fief in southern Hebei founded by a son of the Duke of Zhou, rescued from Di raiders by Qi and finally destroyed by its kinsmen of Wey.
state-of-xing.o: Xing was granted early in the [[s:western-zhou|Western Zhou]] to a son of the Duke of Zhou, a member of the royal Ji clan, as a northern outpost near modern Xingtai in [[e:hebei|Hebei]]. Inscribed bronzes such as the Mai vessels record its rulers' audiences with the Zhou king.
state-of-xing.r: As a frontier state Xing guarded the Zhou world against the Di peoples of the Taihang uplands. Little is known of its internal life beyond the bronzes and brief entries in the Zuo zhuan, which show a typical Zhou aristocratic state organised around its ruling lineage and ancestral temple.
state-of-xing.e: Di attacks overran Xing in the 660s BCE. Duke Huan of Qi led a coalition to rescue it and resettled its people at Yiyi in 659 BCE. Weakened, Xing was annexed in 635 BCE by the [[s:state-of-wey|State of Wey]], a fellow Ji-clan state, which was criticised for destroying kin.

saybrook-colony.t: A short-lived English fort colony at the mouth of the Connecticut River, planned as a refuge for Puritan lords and sold to Connecticut in 1644.
saybrook-colony.o: In 1632 a group of Puritan aristocrats, led by Viscount Saye and Sele and Lord Brooke, obtained the Warwick Patent to land in southern New [[e:england|England]]. In 1635 John Winthrop the Younger, acting as their governor, sent men to build a fort at the mouth of the Connecticut River, named Saybrook after the two patrons.
saybrook-colony.r: The engineer Lion Gardiner built and commanded the fort, which was meant to guard the river and prepare a home for the lords and their followers, who never came. The settlement remained a small garrison with a few families. During the [[s:pequot-nation|Pequot]] War it was besieged by the Pequot Nation in 1636 to 1637 and served as a base for English expeditions. George Fenwick, one of the patentees, later lived there as governor.
saybrook-colony.e: With the English Civil War keeping the patrons at home, Fenwick sold the fort and its land to the [[s:connecticut-colony|Connecticut Colony]] in 1644. The town of Old Saybrook preserves the name.

state-of-sui.t: A Ji-clan state in Hubei, now identified with the Zeng of the bronzes, whose Marquis Yi was buried with the most famous set of chime bells in China.
state-of-sui.o: [[e:sui-dynasty|Sui]] was founded early in the [[s:western-zhou|Western Zhou]] by a branch of the royal Ji clan at Suizhou in northern Hubei, guarding the corridor to the [[e:copper|copper]] mines of the middle [[e:yangtze-river|Yangtze]]. Excavated bronzes call the state Zeng, and most scholars now treat Sui and Zeng as the same state.
state-of-sui.r: In the 8th and 7th centuries BCE [[e:sui-dynasty|Sui]] led the small states of the [[e:han-river|Han River]] region against the [[s:state-of-chu|State of Chu]]; King Wu of Chu died on campaign against it in 690 BCE. It later became a close Chu ally and sheltered King Zhao of Chu when Wu armies took Ying in 506 BCE. The tomb of Marquis Yi of Zeng, buried around 433 BCE, held 65 bronze bells, [[e:lacquerware|lacquerware]] and early writing on bamboo.
state-of-sui.e: [[e:sui-dynasty|Sui]] faded from the record and was absorbed by Chu, probably in the 4th century BCE. The excavation of Marquis Yi's tomb in 1978 transformed knowledge of early Chinese music and court life.

state-of-dai-di.t: A small Di kingdom in the uplands of northern Hebei, destroyed in 457 BCE when Zhao Xiangzi murdered its king at a banquet.
state-of-dai-di.o: Dai was a state of the Di peoples in the upland basins of northern [[e:shanxi|Shanxi]] and [[e:hebei|Hebei]], around modern Yuxian, on the frontier between the Chinese states and the steppe. Its date of origin is unknown; it appears in Chinese sources in the 6th and 5th centuries BCE.
state-of-dai-di.r: Dai was known for its horses and for trade between farmers and herders. Its king married the sister of Zhao Xiangzi, leader of the Zhao lineage of the [[s:state-of-jin|State of Jin]], but little else is recorded of its government.
state-of-dai-di.e: In 457 BCE Zhao Xiangzi invited the king of Dai to a feast and had him killed with a bronze ladle, then annexed Dai; his sister, the queen, is said to have killed herself with a hairpin. Dai became a base of the Zhao family, the future [[s:state-of-zhao|State of Zhao]].

state-of-cambodia.t: The renamed and reformed successor of the People's Republic of Kampuchea, which governed Cambodia during the peace process of 1989 to 1993.
state-of-cambodia.o: In April 1989 the [[s:peoples-republic-of-kampuchea|People's Republic of Kampuchea]] renamed itself the State of [[s:kingdom-of-cambodia|Cambodia]], restored [[e:buddhism|Buddhism]] as the state religion, reintroduced private property and adopted a new flag, as Vietnamese troops completed their withdrawal in September 1989.
state-of-cambodia.r: The ruling party, renamed the Cambodian People's Party in 1991, governed under Heng Samrin and Prime Minister Hun Sen while negotiating with the resistance factions. The [[e:paris|Paris]] Peace Agreements of October 1991 set up a Supreme National Council chaired by Sihanouk and placed [[s:kingdom-of-cambodia|Cambodia]] under the [[e:united-nations|United Nations]] Transitional Authority in [[e:cambodia|Cambodia]], UNTAC, which oversaw elections.
state-of-cambodia.e: The UN-run elections of May 1993 were won by Prince Norodom Ranariddh's royalist FUNCINPEC party, with the CPP second. A new constitution restored the monarchy, and the State of [[s:kingdom-of-cambodia|Cambodia]] gave way to the Kingdom of [[e:cambodia|Cambodia]] in September 1993.

second-philippine-republic.t: Republic set up by Japan in occupied Philippines under Jose P. Laurel, whose legitimacy remains debated.
second-philippine-republic.o: After occupying [[e:manila|Manila]] in January 1942, [[e:japan|Japan]] governed through a Philippine Executive Commission led by Jorge Vargas. Seeking local support, it granted nominal independence, and on 14 October 1943 the Second [[s:first-philippine-republic|Philippine Republic]] was inaugurated with Jose P. Laurel as president under a new constitution.
second-philippine-republic.r: Laurel tried to shield Filipinos from harsher Japanese demands and resisted conscription, but real power lay with the Japanese army, and food shortages and atrocities fuelled resentment. Widespread [[e:guerrilla-warfare|guerrilla]] resistance loyal to the [[s:commonwealth-of-the-philippines|Commonwealth of the Philippines]] government in exile continued. In September 1944 the republic declared war on the [[s:united-states|United States]] and [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]].
second-philippine-republic.e: As American forces returned in 1944 and 1945, Laurel fled to [[e:japan|Japan]] and dissolved the republic on 17 August 1945. Its leaders faced collaboration charges but were amnestied in 1948, and Laurel is now counted among Philippine presidents.

suphannaphum.t: A Thai kingdom west of the Chao Phraya, centred on Suphanburi, whose ruling house took over Ayutthaya and swallowed Sukhothai.
suphannaphum.o: Suphannaphum emerged as a Tai polity around Suphanburi in the 12th century, in an area earlier settled by [[s:dvaravati|Dvaravati]] communities. Chinese records of missions from Xian, often taken to mean this region, suggest a growing Thai power in the lower Chao Phraya by the late 13th century.
suphannaphum.r: The kingdom was based on [[e:rice|rice]] farming and trade along the western rivers. Its royal house, sometimes called the Suphannaphum dynasty, intermarried with Lavo. After U Thong founded [[s:ayutthaya-kingdom|Ayutthaya]] in 1351, Khun Luang Pa-ngua of Suphanburi, his brother-in-law, seized the [[e:ayutthaya-kingdom|Ayutthaya]] throne in 1370 as Borommarachathirat I and campaigned against [[s:sukhothai-kingdom|Sukhothai]].
suphannaphum.e: Suphannaphum effectively merged with [[s:ayutthaya-kingdom|Ayutthaya]], whose kings from Intharacha onward were of its line. In 1438 Borommarachathirat II absorbed the [[s:sukhothai-kingdom|Sukhothai Kingdom]], and Suphanburi became a provincial city of [[e:ayutthaya-kingdom|Ayutthaya]]. Its rulers had thus shaped the core of the later Siamese state.

sovereign-principality-of-the-united-net.t: The transitional Dutch state of 1813–1815, created as Napoleon's empire collapsed, under the returning Prince of Orange as sovereign prince.
sovereign-principality-of-the-united-net.o: After [[e:napoleon|Napoleon's]] defeat at Leipzig, French authority in the [[s:kingdom-of-the-netherlands|Netherlands]] collapsed in November 1813. A provisional government led by Gijsbert Karel van Hogendorp invited William Frederick, son of the last stadtholder, to return. He landed at Scheveningen on 30 November and accepted the title of sovereign prince.
sovereign-principality-of-the-united-net.r: William ruled under a new constitution adopted in 1814, which gave the sovereign wide powers while keeping a States General. The new state rejected the old federal republic in favour of the unitary government created in the Batavian period. Its priority was rebuilding finances and securing allied backing at the [[e:congress-of-vienna|Congress of Vienna]].
sovereign-principality-of-the-united-net.e: The great powers decided to unite the northern and southern [[s:kingdom-of-the-netherlands|Netherlands]] as a barrier to [[e:france|France]]. In March 1815, during [[e:napoleon|Napoleon's]] [[e:hundred-days-reform|Hundred Days]], William proclaimed himself king, creating the [[s:united-kingdom-of-the-netherlands|United Kingdom of the Netherlands]].

sonargaon-sultanate.t: An independent Muslim sultanate of eastern Bengal, the first to break from the Delhi Sultanate, ruled by Fakhruddin Mubarak Shah.
sonargaon-sultanate.o: In 1338 Fakhruddin Mubarak Shah, an armour-bearer of the Tughluq governor of Sonargaon, seized power after his master's death and declared independence from Muhammad bin Tughluq. He held eastern [[e:bengal|Bengal]] from Sonargaon while rival rulers controlled Lakhnauti and Satgaon in the west.
sonargaon-sultanate.r: Fakhruddin built roads and mosques and expanded control towards Chittagong, one of the earliest Muslim conquests of that port. He issued coins in his own name, a key source for the period. [[e:ibn-battuta|Ibn Battuta]] passed through his territory in 1346 and noted the abundance and cheapness of [[e:rice|rice]] and goods.
sonargaon-sultanate.e: Fakhruddin was succeeded by his son Ikhtiyaruddin [[e:ghazi|Ghazi]] Shah. In 1352 Shamsuddin Ilyas Shah of Lakhnauti conquered Sonargaon, uniting all of [[e:bengal|Bengal]] under the [[s:bengal-sultanate|Bengal Sultanate]]. Sonargaon remained an important city and mint town.

satake-clan-domain.t: The domain of the Satake of Hitachi, an old warrior house that dominated northeastern Kanto in the Sengoku period before its transfer to Akita in 1602.
satake-clan-domain.o: The Satake, a branch of the Seiwa Genji, had been established in Hitachi since the 12th century. After long internal conflicts, they restored their unity around 1500 and from their castle at Ota expanded across the province.
satake-clan-domain.r: Satake Yoshishige, nicknamed the demon of Hitachi, fought the Later Hojo for control of the northern Kanto and allied with neighbours to resist them. His son Yoshinobu supported [[e:toyotomi-hideyoshi|Toyotomi Hideyoshi]], joined the siege of Odawara in 1590, and was confirmed in a large fief across Hitachi, moving his seat to Mito.
satake-clan-domain.e: Yoshinobu remained neutral at [[e:battle-of-sekigahara|Sekigahara]] in 1600, and [[e:tokugawa-ieyasu|Tokugawa Ieyasu]] punished him in 1602 by transferring the clan to the much smaller [[s:kubota-domain|Kubota Domain]] in Dewa, where the Satake ruled until 1871.

sint-eustatius.t: Tiny Dutch island that became the busiest free port of the 18th-century Caribbean and gave the first foreign salute to the flag of the United States.
sint-eustatius.o: [[s:county-of-zeeland|Zeeland]] settlers founded a colony on Sint Eustatius in 1636 and built Fort Oranje above the harbour at Oranjestad. The island changed hands between the [[e:dutch|Dutch]], English and French many times in the 17th century before settling under the [[e:dutch-west-india-company|Dutch West India Company]].
sint-eustatius.r: With little farmland, Statia thrived as a neutral free port where goods of every nation were traded, including arms, [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]] and enslaved people. Its Lower Town was lined with warehouses, and the island had a [[e:dutch|Dutch]] Reformed church, a Jewish congregation and a polyglot merchant class. On 16 November 1776 Fort Oranje returned the salute of the American brig Andrew Doria, the first recognition of the new republic's flag.
sint-eustatius.e: [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] declared war on the [[s:dutch-republic|Dutch Republic]] in 1780, and Admiral George Rodney seized and plundered the island in 1781. Its trade never recovered. After further occupations, [[e:dutch|Dutch]] rule was restored in 1816, and in 1845 the island was placed under the colony of [[s:colony-of-curacao|Curaçao and Dependencies]]. It is now a special municipality of the [[s:kingdom-of-the-netherlands|Netherlands]].

shahpura-state.t: A small Sisodia Rajput state of Rajasthan, centre of the Ramsnehi sect and home of the painted Phad scrolls.
shahpura-state.o: Shahpura was granted in 1629 by the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan to Sujan Singh, of the Ranawat branch of the Sisodia house of [[s:udaipur-state|Mewar]]. The town is named after the emperor. The rulers also held lands from Mewar, which created a long dispute over their status.
shahpura-state.r: The Rajadhirajs ruled a small territory near Bhilwara. Shahpura became the headquarters of the Ramsnehi devotional sect, founded in the 18th century, and the home of the Joshi painters of Phad, long cloth scrolls used by bards narrating the epics of folk deities.
shahpura-state.e: Shahpura joined the [[s:united-state-of-rajasthan|United State of Rajasthan]] in 1948. The town, in Bhilwara district, remains a Ramsnehi pilgrimage centre and the heart of Phad painting.

soviet-civil-administration.t: The Soviet occupation authority in northern Korea from 1945 to 1948, which brought Kim Il Sung to power and built the foundations of North Korea.
soviet-civil-administration.o: The [[s:soviet-union|Soviet Union]] declared war on [[e:japan|Japan]] in August 1945, and its 25th Army under General Ivan Chistyakov swept into northern [[e:korea|Korea]]. Under a hastily agreed line, Soviet forces occupied the peninsula north of the 38th parallel, and a civil administration was set up in Pyongyang to govern it.
soviet-civil-administration.r: Soviet officers, overseen by Colonel General Terentii Shtykov, ruled indirectly through local people's committees, sidelining nationalists such as Cho Man-sik. They promoted Kim Il Sung, a former [[e:guerrilla-warfare|guerrilla]] officer, and backed the [[s:provisional-peoples-committee-for-north-korea|Provisional People's Committee for North Korea]], which carried out land reform and nationalised industry. Japanese property and some industrial plant were seized.
soviet-civil-administration.e: Talks with the [[s:united-states|United States]] on a unified government failed. The Democratic [[s:peoples-republic-of-korea|People's Republic of Korea]] was proclaimed in September 1948 with Kim Il Sung as premier, and Soviet troops withdrew by the end of that year.

sri-lanka.t: The island republic of the Indian Ocean, which emerged from a 26-year civil war in 2009.
sri-lanka.o: The constitution of 1972 ended the [[s:dominion-of-ceylon|Dominion of Ceylon]] and renamed the country Sri Lanka, giving [[e:buddhism|Buddhism]] a foremost place. In 1978 J. R. Jayewardene introduced an executive presidency, and the administrative capital moved to Sri Jayawardenepura [[s:kingdom-of-kotte|Kotte]], near Colombo.
sri-lanka.r: Jayewardene's government opened the economy, but anti-Tamil riots in 1983 began a civil war with the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam seeking a Tamil state in the north and east. Indian peacekeepers intervened from 1987 to 1990, and a second JVP insurrection was crushed. [[e:tea|Tea]], garments and tourism drove the economy. The Sri Lankan army defeated the Tigers in 2009 at great civilian cost.
sri-lanka.e: The republic continues. A debt crisis in 2022 led to mass protests and the resignation of President Gotabaya Rajapaksa, and in 2024 Anura Kumara Dissanayake of the left-wing NPP alliance was elected president.
